You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaperTest.testUnfinishedEntity()
  - Input: "Test &#x30 not test" (no terminating semicolon)
  - Expected (by test variable): "Test \u0030 not test" (i.e., the numeric entity decoded even without a trailing ‘;’)
  - Actual: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown.

- Relevant execution flow:
  - CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, Writer) iterates over the input and delegates to NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(CharSequence, int, Writer) for each code point.
  - In NumericEntityUnescaper.translate:
    - It detects sequences starting with "&#" (lines 40–41).
    - Determines hex mode if an 'x' or 'X' follows (lines 44–48), then sets start to the first digit (after '&#x').
    - It then scans for the end of the entity using:
      while (input.charAt(end) != ';') { end++; } (lines 54–57)

- Root cause:
  - The loop at lines 54–57 assumes a terminating semicolon and never checks bounds. If no semicolon is present (unfinished entity), end increments until it equals input.length(), and the next input.charAt(end) access throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.
  - This directly matches the bug report (“StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when calling unescapeHtml4("&#03")”) because "&#03" has no semicolon and triggers the same faulty loop.
  - Additional out-of-bounds risk: When the input ends right after "&#" (e.g., "Test &#"), start == input.length() and charAt(start) at line 44 throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The testOutOfBounds() hints this case should be ignored (return original text), but current code does not guard for it.
  - The method also claims to “support character codes without a ; on the end” (comment at line 53), but the implementation contradicts this: it only searches for a semicolon and never stops on non-digit/non-hex characters or end-of-input. The return-length computation (line 80) always adds +1 for a semicolon, which would be incorrect even if the loop were bounds-safe.

- How the failure happens for the failing test input:
  - Input: "Test &#x30 not test"
  - At the '&' index, condition matches. isHex = true; start points to '3'. end starts at start and increments through '3', '0', ' ' (space), 'n', ... until it reaches the end of the string without encountering ';'. When end == input.length(), the next input.charAt(end) access at line 54 throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.
  - Therefore, the test fails due to the unguarded while loop and lack of handling for unfinished entities.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
